title: Create an organization and wait
description:
**Phase 4 of 7.**

- **Blocked by:** 22f5bb
- **Runs in parallel with:** 7b4616
- **Unblocks:** ae51dc

---
Anyone signing in may create an organization, which lands it pending, and sees the welcome screen. Google sign-in is the waitlist form: the address is verified, there is no form backend and no spam, and enabling later is a flag flip on an account that already exists.

Do not show a queue position. It implies an ordering that will not be honored, because organizations are chosen deliberately. Do not promise an email unless SES is out of the sandbox; at this volume, mail the owner by hand when their organization is enabled.

**Done when:** a new person can sign in, create an organization, and see the welcome screen, and an operator sees it via the members CLI.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Signup openness becomes deployment configuration.**

The three-level model changes what this card means. A deployment is one customer company; tenants are departments inside it. So open signup is right for the Anthus deployment, where anyone may sign in and ask for a tenant, and wrong for a customer deployment, where members are that company's employees and enablement belongs to their own admin.

**Do not hardcode open signup.** The deployment configures whether sign-in creates a pending tenant or refuses anyone without an invitation. Both paths already exist in this epic; this is a switch over which one is reachable, not new machinery.

Same applies to ae51dc: invitation-only is the default posture for a customer deployment, and open signup is the exception the Anthus deployment turns on.
